chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: World War I: no war material in the act, and too young to enlist
summary: He did not add war material to his act and was only 15 when the war was on; he says no one specific shaped his development.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Was it -- this was during World War I?
So there was a lot of entertainment gearing itself around the war, too.
Were you, in your own act, were you doing stuff that was geared towards the war?
No, I was just doing the act. No do no stuff towards the war. Just doing the act.
You didn't add any different additional routines?
So basically the kind of comedy that they were doing, this now during the 20's, some of them were still doing war.

Well, the gag that they used on little bits concerning the army. It wasn't going out doing an act concerning the army, the war or nothing like that. They'd do bits of the army that you wouldn't ordinarily do just dry long so. You got to build it like you build a sketch of anything. They do the hospital bit now but in the act it's just a bit they do from the hospital. This is the kind of thing they did.
Were there any specific people at that time that were
playing an important role in your own develop- ment as an entertainer?

No. Just that there were entertainers, I'm not the only entertainer -- Buck and I weren't the only entertainers. There were plenty of entertainers. They had a variety act of maybe 8 or 9 acts on the bill, 6 or 7 acts, something like that.
